1. The present appeal is filed by the original claimant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 26.7.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi),
Jamnagar in MACP No.752 of 1999.

2. Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellant - original claimant under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellant- original claimant entitled to an amount of Rs.33,750/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.
Thus, the Tribunal has not entertained the claim petition for an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- as total compensation.

3. The brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1
On 17.08.1988, the claimant was travelling from his village Sonvadiya to Jamjodhpur in a Rickshaw bearing No. GRT 4828 for visiting the Doctor along with his goods for farming.
When the Rickshaw reached near the crossing of village Jamvadi, one another Rickshaw bearing No. GJ 13 T 5612 came from the opposite direction.
The driver of the said Rickshaw, due to rash and negligent driving, collided with the Rickshaw in which the claimant was a passenger.
3.2 As a result of the collision, the claimant sustained serious injuries.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Rickshaw.
At the time of the accident, the claimant was 21 years old, physically healthy, and working as an agricultural labourer earning 2,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he suffered a fracture in his right leg and serious injuries to other parts NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/283/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined of his body.
He was immediately taken to Jamjodhpur Government Hospital for treatment.
After primary treatment, he was shifted to Irwin Hospital, Jamnagar for further treatment.
Even after prolonged treatment, the claimant was unable to resume agricultural work, and due to the accident, he had to incur considerable expenses and has suffered permanent disability.

3.3 Therefore, the appellant - claimant has filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- with cost and interest for the injuries sustained by the appellant - claimant against the respondents before the Tribunal.
3.4 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
4. This Court vide order dated 05.03.2014 noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant-original claimant and the grounds raised in the appeal, has admitted the appeal.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Makbul I. Mansuri, appearing for the appellant, while assailing the impugned judgment, has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimant and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.

It is contended that the Tribunal has not NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/283/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined properly assessed the income of the appellant as well as period of actual loss of income, and has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to the assessment of future prospects and grant of compensation under the various heads such as special diet and actual loss of income along with rate of interest.
6. It is further submitted that the Tribunal has awarded a meager and unrealistic amount under various heads without considering the socio-economic background of the appellant.
The learned counsel has urged that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable, and is liable to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles.
Learned counsel therefore prays for enhancement of the compensation amount by reassessing the same in accordance with law.

7. Learned advocate Mr. G.C. Mazmudar appearing for the respondent No.2 and 5 - Insurance Company has placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and vehemently argued that the compensation must be awarded as just, proper and reasonable and not higher side and further submitted that learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record, awarded the compensation under each head is just, proper and reasonable and not required to interfere and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/283/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined

8. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation.
9.
As regards the income of the appellant is concerned, the appellant was working as an agricultural worker at the time of the accident.

The tribunal has erred in assessing Rs.15,000/- per annum (Rs.
1250/-pm) towards the income of the appellant.
Considering the nature of work with which the appellant is associated, it would be just and proper to assess the income of the appellant as Rs.1800/- per month.
10. As regards the injury and disability sustained by the appellant, both the parties consented to assess the disability at 5%.
Hence, as the disability was assessed by consent, there is no dispute raised in that regard and 5% disability is required to be applied while calculating the compensation.

11. As regards future rise of income is concerned, the age of the appellant, the injury sustained by him and that he was working as an agricultural worker at the time of the accident is required to be taken in to consideration.
From the evidence, the said injury has affected the future earning capacity of the appellant.

Considering the nature of his work and injury sustained, and in view of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/283/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi,

12. Noticing the fact that the appellant was aged 21 years at the time of accident, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the schedule prescribed, the Tribunal has rightly considered applying the multiplier of 18.

Thus, the future loss benefit is determined as Rs.1512/-*18 (Multiplier) which comes to Rs.27,216/-.
13.

So far as the compensation under the other heads such as pain, shock and suffering and special diet, attendant charges and transportation are concerned, considering the facts of the case, nature of injuries, medical treatment and physical pain and the emotional trauma endured by the appellant,
some enhancement under the abovementioned heads are deserves to be enhanced.

Accordingly,
Rs.5,000/- towards Special Diet, Attendance Charges and Transportation, etc. are required to be given.
The medical expenses of Rs.3000/- awarded by the tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/283/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined required under that head.

Moreover, under the head of actual loss of income, towards which Rs. 1,250/- is awarded only is required to be enhanced to Rs. 5,400/- towards actual loss of income for three months as per the enhanced income.

14. As held in the fatal case of a co-passenger of the appellant - claimant whose legal heirs preferred First Appeal No. 1682 of 2010, the Coordinate Bench of this Court passed the oral order on dated 25.09.2024 and on note for speaking to minutes of order dated 25.09.2024 on dated 21.01.2025, the Insurance Company was held liable and was held entitled to recover the amount from the concerned driver and owner of the vehicle.

Hence, the rate of interest awarded by the learned Tribunal is also required to be enhanced from the rate of 7% to 7.5%.
15.

Therefore, original claimant - appellant herein is entitled to enhanced amount as computed hereunder:

16.
For the foregoing reasons, the impugned judgment and award dated 26.7.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi), Jamnagar in MACP No.752 of 1999 is hereby modified.
The appellant-original claimant is held entitled to compensation of an amount of Rs.50,616/-.

Since by impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.33,750/-, the appellant shall be entitled to enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.16,866/- (Rs.50,616/- -
Rs.33,750/-) with interest at the rate of 7.5% from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization.
The respondent - Insurance Company is held liable to pay such enhanced amount of compensation with proportionate costs and interest.

17. Let, the aforesaid amount be deposited with the concerned Tribunal within a period of 8 weeks from the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/283/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined date of receipt of the present order.

On deposit of the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall be at liberty to release and disburse the entire award amount in favour of the original claimant, after due Naran Khimji Harijan vs Bihari Babulal on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143769177/
